stem: A healthcare study measures average patient recovery rate across 5 hospitals, each containing multiple departments. hospital A has 20 observations with mean 49.1 % (within-hospital SD = 6.3). hospital B has 15 observations with mean 36.1 % (within-hospital SD = 9.6). hospital C has 5 observations with mean 37.3 % (within-hospital SD = 8.0). hospital D has 20 observations with mean 46.5 % (within-hospital SD = 4.6). hospital E has 10 observations with mean 46.0 % (within-hospital SD = 9.6). The between-hospital standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 5.3 and 13.2 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true average patient recovery rate for hospital C, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-hospital variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for hospital C: 38.3 % (shrunk from raw 37.3). Range [37.8, 39.5] as between-hospital SD varies from 5.3 to 13.2. Pooled mean: 44.3.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 44.3 % (weighted average of 5 hospital means).
Shrinkage factor for hospital C: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/5). At σ_between=8.8: B = 0.858.
Interval [37.8, 39.5] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (37.3) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (44.3) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
